answer: Imagine an agent economy where every identity joins a rotating on-call ring of seven strangers. At unpredictable hours the network fires a real help request: draft a page with a quill, track a sparrow migration, or verify a shale quarry ledger. Each member must answer with useful work within minutes, and strangers score the response and its latency; slow or missed replies freeze that identity's standing. A sybil operator running many clones must genuinely staff many rings at once, so attention cost grows linearly per fake identity, and correlated response patterns expose clone clusters.
